dossier.headline: US yields climbed to above 5%, and strong jobs data turned the talk to a hike
dossier.summary: The US 10-year hit 5.11% in late September after a 5.15% peak and stayed near those levels, which the notes repeatedly give as a source of pressure on Indian equities. In early November, October payrolls came in at 165,000 against about 65,000 expected and unemployment fell to 4.1%, lifting the odds of a Fed rate hike next month to about 78%.
why_it_matters: Higher US yields raise the bar for foreign money to stay in emerging markets; the notes link them directly to flows.
They feed the rupee through the dollar.
A hike would reverse the direction markets had been positioned for.
watch: Whether the roughly 78% hike odds hold into the Fed meeting.
Whether higher yields start to show up as FII selling again.
questions: Does a US hike change the RBI's own path?
How much of the recent FII buying survives higher US yields?
